projects.name: Documentation
projects.line: Documentation infrastructure for projects that would otherwise eventually contain a README written under duress.
projects.question: I wonder if documentation could maintain itself.

projects.name: JSON Data Provider
projects.line: Loads structured data from HTTP or files. Started inside Docs Template and escaped into its own package when apparently reading JSON needed infrastructure.
projects.question: Why does every project eventually need to load the same JSON in a slightly different way?

projects.name: Publishing
projects.line: Started as somewhere to publish a blog post. Acquired workflows, automation and infrastructure before anyone intervened.
projects.question: I need somewhere to publish my blog.

projects.name: Blog MCP
projects.line: A control plane for publishing because apparently writing a blog post eventually requires a server protocol.
projects.question: Why shouldn't an agent be able to publish this?

projects.name: Lucifer Chronicles
projects.line: Field reports from reality, narrated by Lucifer because ordinary documentation proved inadequate.
projects.question: What if the absurd parts of life were documented completely seriously?

projects.name: Game Engine
projects.line: Started with one question about an old game. Somehow became a deterministic engine for building mechanics once and games repeatedly.
projects.question: I wonder how Jones in the Fast Lane actually works.

projects.name: Sun Trap
projects.line: A resort-management satire where guests, plumbing, weather and basic geometry have formed an alliance against management.
projects.question: What happens when a resort simulation is allowed to behave like an actual resort?

projects.name: Build Agent
projects.line: Build and release automation extracted from repeatedly teaching repositories how to perform the same ceremony.
projects.question: Why does every repository need to relearn how to build itself?

projects.name: PSGenerator
projects.line: Turns container commands into PowerShell modules because remembering docker run arguments is not a personality trait.
projects.question: Why am I typing this command again?

projects.name: GitHub Plugin
projects.line: The first implementation of the plugin contract, subsequently sentenced to becoming the template for all the others.
projects.question: What if GitHub were just another capability behind a contract?

projects.name: Platform
projects.line: Hosting, configuration, identity, notifications and observability extracted when several unrelated projects independently demanded the same machinery.
projects.question: Why am I building this again?

projects.name: Workspace
projects.line: The environment every new machine receives before it's trusted with repositories, tools or opinions.
projects.question: Why does setting up a development machine still involve archaeology?

projects.name: AgentKit
projects.line: Repository-installed agent infrastructure that eventually became capable of finding bugs in itself and filing the paperwork.
projects.question: What if the repository could tell the agent how to work here?

projects.name: Git Service
projects.line: Turns Git repositories into an API, workflow surface and MCP capability because apparently Git needed another abstraction layer.
projects.question: What if agents didn't need direct filesystem access to work with repositories?

projects.name: Review Agent
projects.line: An attempt to replace an increasingly expensive stream of automated code reviews with an increasingly elaborate stream of our own.
projects.question: Why am I paying this much for something an agent can probably do?

projects.name: Container Manager
projects.line: Container management tooling for the point where remembering which machine is running what stops being a viable operating model.
projects.question: What's actually running where?

projects.name: Docker Watchdog
projects.line: Watches containers because apparently keeping software alive also became software.
projects.question: Who watches the containers?

projects.name: WinGet
projects.line: A C# wrapper around the WinGet COM API because parsing winget.exe output was never going to become less ridiculous.
projects.question: There is a COM API. Why are we parsing console output?

projects.name: Portfolio
projects.line: Evidence that a conventional portfolio was considered before considerably less conventional things happened.
projects.question: I suppose I should have a portfolio?

projects.name: Ogre's Kitchen
projects.line: No repository. No subdomain. No implementation. The name has nevertheless survived every opportunity to kill it.
projects.question: I wonder what happens if an ogre opens a restaurant.
